Chapter 250: 0247 Youke is Developing Three Games at Once?

Chen Guilang did a round of the various booths and found that there were quite a few games self-developed or licensed by major companies this year.

These games were being promoted at the ChinaJoy Digital Entertainment Expo before they had even launched.

There were also foreign companies that had come to sell their games, like *Dungeon & Fighter*!

"Our *DNF* is already ranked in the top three for play rate in South Korean PC bangs, and its ranking continues to rise. More and more Korean players are choosing *DNF* because of our unique..." a Korean man explained to Chinese companies and reporters with a translator.

When promoting a game, of course, you only talk about the good parts, not the bad.

In the first three months of *DNF*'s open beta in South Korea, it was nothing short of a game operation disaster. When concurrent users exceeded 100,000, the Korean servers crashed.

They finally managed to get the servers sorted out, only for instant-kill full-screen hacks and invincibility hacks to become rampant. The player churn rate once reached 40%.

Just a short while ago, they banned 120,000 hacked accounts in one go!

The unlucky things Tencent encountered in the early days of licensing *DNF* were merely a repeat of *DNF*'s disaster in South Korea.

Representatives from The9 Game were the first to make contact regarding *DNF*.

They went to a negotiation room provided by the exhibition organizer for a private chat.

"We at The9 are quite interested in *DNF*. What is your price for the licensing rights?"

"A signing fee of 500,000 USD, a minimum guaranteed share of 800,000 USD, and a 35% licensing share..."

"Thank you, we still need to evaluate this game."

The9's representative only made simple contact, asked for the price, and then left. Whether to license the game still required a company meeting and vote.

Immediately after, more than ten Chinese licensing companies, including Optic Communications, Shanda, Tencent, and 9you, went to inquire one after another.

This gave the developers of *DNF* a false impression that the Chinese game companies were extremely optimistic, as if they would die if they didn't license their game.

Thus, just a few days later, when The9 negotiated with the Korean side again, the Koreans suddenly asked for an exorbitant price.

The signing fee was raised from 500,000 USD to 2 million.

The annual minimum guaranteed share was raised from 800,000 USD to 2 million.

What was even more ridiculous was that they came up with a 5 million USD source code deposit. This was to prevent the Chinese licensee from leaking the source code, and the money would only be returned at the end of the contract period.

Absolutely insane!

When The9's boss, Zhu Jun, received the report over the phone, he was stunned for a moment by the Korean side's demands, and then he cursed, "A 5 million dollar deposit is enough to sign a *World of Warcraft* expansion! Call our people back. Stop the negotiations."

And so, The9 was the first to pull out.

NetEase was the second to pull out.

The other Chinese companies, however, were still in talks with the Koreans. They said they didn't mind the last-minute price gouging, as they had seen the Korean side renege on deals many times before.

Everyone knew what the Koreans were like!

It was nothing more than asking for the sky and settling for less.

The reason The9 and NetEase couldn't be bothered to continue talks was that they had *World of Warcraft* and *Fantasy Westward Journey* on their hands. They had no need to put up with the Koreans' nonsense.

Chen Guilang also went to ask about it.

When he sent someone to make contact for the second time, the Korean side's shameless demand of a price hike made Chen Guilang laugh in anger.

Ever since online games appeared in mainland China, no one had ever heard of a source code deposit. And for 5 million USD!

You had to admire the Koreans' imagination.

Chen Guilang discussed this matter with Tao Chenggang, and Tao Chenggang was also amused. "Are they f*cking crazy? Leaving 5 million USD sitting there for several years is like giving the Koreans an interest-free loan. Not even *World of Warcraft* was this arrogant. Who gave the Koreans the guts to make such a demand?"

Chen Guilang said with a smile, "The Korean side also demanded that a 15-person Korean team be stationed at the licensee's company. The annual salary and travel expenses of 3 million yuan would have to be paid by the Chinese licensee."

"Hahaha!" Tao Chenggang burst out laughing when he heard this.

Even a company like Tencent wouldn't agree to such absurd demands.

That was why Tencent ended up haggling with the Koreans for over a year. It was only after the other potential licensees gradually dropped out that the Korean side was finally willing to yield.

Back to the day of the exhibition.

Chen Guilang strolled back to his own company's booth and found that there was actually a queue of people waiting to play a game.

It was a small Flash game: *Rampage Kids*.

The first version of this thing had been released abroad as early as 2003, with the official version launching in 2005.

Chen Guilang didn't just localize and copy it directly. Instead, he kept its core satisfying elements and remade it with a new look.

This way, there would be no copyright disputes.

He couldn't even be bothered to make it himself, so he outsourced it directly. The outsourcing fee was only 35,000 yuan.

If he had only wanted a crude version, 5,000 yuan would have been enough.

Chen Guilang never thought about making money from *Rampage Kids*; it was purely to be put on the Youke Huyu platform to attract some traffic.

He even deliberately added a line of text at the beginning of the game: A grateful tribute to the original foreign version, *Dad 'n Me*.

"President Chen, this little game of yours is so satisfying!" a reporter from 17173 said while playing.

Chen Guilang said, "It's actually more suitable for adults. Work and life are stressful, and this little game can relieve that stress. I'm just afraid someone will nitpick and say I'm promoting violence and being a bad influence on children."

The reporter laughed, "It really could be a bad influence on children!"

The guy grabbed a kid from the roadside and threw him onto the main road to be hit by a car.

There was nothing complicated about *Rampage Kids*. You just walked down the street and beat up anyone you saw.

It was incredibly stress-relieving, releasing the destructive desires buried deep in the human heart.

The reporter played for a few minutes, then got up to let others in the queue have a turn, and came over to do an exclusive interview with Chen Guilang.

Reporter: First of all, congratulations, President Chen. Both *Sanguosha* and *Reign of Power* have achieved impressive results.

Chen Guilang: Thank you.

Reporter: What are your plans for the future? Is it alright to ask about that?

Chen Guilang: To do a good job with *Sanguosha*, Youfutong, and Youke Huyu. The number of registered users on Youke Huyu has already reached 6 million. Our various small games are very popular, and our chess and card games have also started to turn a profit. As for the Youfutong payment system, besides Youke using it ourselves, Xiaonei, Hainei, and *Reign of Power* are also using it. In addition, two other small game companies have also chosen to partner with Youfutong.

Reporter: Do you have any plans to develop or license new games? *DNF* is very popular today. I heard more than ten companies went to make inquiries.

Chen Guilang: I also contacted the developers of *DNF*. But I promised last year that I would not license Korean games.

Reporter: President Chen is a man of his word. I'm impressed.

Chen Guilang: I bought the game adaptation rights for *My Own Swordsman*. The project has already been greenlit. Moreover, Ning Caishen, the screenwriter of *My Own Swordsman*, will be one of the planners for the game of the same name.

Reporter: This is big news. *My Own Swordsman* has been popular since the beginning of the year, and it's still being broadcast on loop on some local TV stations. Its online download and viewership numbers are also very high. When can we expect the game of the same name to be released?

Chen Guilang: It's hard to say. I strive for excellence when making games, so it might take one and a half to two years.

Reporter: That is indeed striving for excellence. Few self-developed games in China take more than a year. Any game with a development cycle longer than a year is bound to be a high-quality product.

Chen Guilang: Actually, Youke has another game that has been in development for nearly a year. And we are also developing our own game engine at the same time, so the development progress is relatively slow.

Reporter: President Chen, you really have a lot of patience. If it were any other company, a game with a development time of nearly a year would already be in open beta. You haven't even started promoting it or revealed any information.

Chen Guilang: Isn't this the start of the promotion?

Reporter: What is the name of the game?

Chen Guilang: *Future Era*. The game is set in a future where a cataclysm has occurred, and human civilization has regressed to the Middle Ages. All sorts of modern technology no longer exist; they can only produce simple guns and cannons. At the same time, spiritual energy has been revived, leading to the appearance of cultivators and mages.

Reporter: That sounds very interesting.

Reporter: President Chen, you are very ambitious. For your company's second game, you're actually developing your own engine.

Chen Guilang: There are no usable commercial engines on the market.

Reporter: How can that be? Is there some kind of novel game content?

Chen Guilang: That's a secret. Actually, Youke is also about to make a small standalone game.

Reporter: You're already making *Future Era*, have greenlit *My Own Swordsman*, and now you're making a standalone game? Three new games at the same time.

Chen Guilang: That's right. The small standalone game is called *Plants vs. Zombies*.

Reporter: Standalone games don't make money these days, do they? Most of the studios or companies that used to make standalone games have now switched to making online games.

Chen Guilang: Someone has to keep making standalone games.

The reporter was deeply shocked. He felt he had struck gold with this interview, managing to get so much information out of Chen Guilang in one go.

Chen Guilang actually felt quite helpless.

Due to technical limitations, *Plants vs. Zombies* could be made as a Flash game, but then it wouldn't be possible to save progress. You'd have to start from the first level every time.

It could barely be made as a web game, but it would be extremely prone to crashing in the middle of playing.

He could only give up on the web version, just like with *Sanguosha*, and make it directly as a standalone client-based game.

Piracy was rampant for standalone games, so Chen Guilang couldn't be bothered to sell physical installation versions.

So, he would put it on the Youke Huyu platform, with the first few levels being playable. If you wanted to continue playing, you could get a key for 5 yuan.

He estimated that it wouldn't be long before a cracked version appeared online.

It was uncertain whether he could even recoup his costs.

After a year and a half, when cracked versions were everywhere, the price of the official version would be directly reduced to 1 yuan. At the same time, new levels and items would be introduced to maintain a sense of superiority for official users.

The time when *Plants vs. Zombies* would truly make money was when it could be made into a web game. The time it could make big money, however, would have to wait until the era of mobile games.

Making it as a standalone client game now was simply to secure this IP in advance!

In any case, the development costs weren't high.

The next day, the first batch of reports from 17173's special coverage of the ChinaJoy Digital Entertainment Expo was released.

The news about Game Science was very eye-catching among these reports.

The headline was: *Youke Enters Overdrive, Announces Simultaneous Development of Three New Games*

"Yesterday, this reporter interviewed Youke founder Chen Guilang, who stated... One of the games, *Future Era*, is very mysterious. It has been in development for nearly a year, and the company is also developing its own game engine. One of the planners is the great online novelist, author of *Chronicles of the Soulless*, Shu Xia Ye Hu, and the novel of the same name is already being serialized on Qidian."

"The second game is *My Own Swordsman*, with the original screenwriter of the TV series serving as the literary planner..."

"The third is even a standalone game..."

As soon as the news came out, it caused a sensation in the industry.

It was a real sensation. Even the giants of the domestic game industry had been keeping a close eye on Chen Guilang.

Because *Sanguosha* and *Reign of Power* were too successful.

Now that Youke was developing three new games at once, and one of them was even a standalone game, this inevitably drew the serious attention of the major companies.

Especially *My Own Swordsman*; that IP alone could be a gold mine.

In the words of a reporter from *Computer World*, the industry was shouting that the wolf was at the door!

(End of this chapter)
